subject: Renewal: Axiom Health — SLA & support upgrade options
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@axiomhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@axiomhealth.com
Date: 2028-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: Axiom Health — SLA & support upgrade options

Evan / Axiom procurement team,

Thanks again for the thoughtful conversation last week. As your renewal approaches (coverage period ending 2028-04-30), I pulled together two reasonable paths to upgrade your SLA and support posture depending on how aggressive you want to be on latency and on-call guarantees. Attached is a one-sheet (SLA_Options_AX-8791.xlsx). High level: 

Option A — Premium SLO: 99.9% p99 latency target, 15-minute P1 response, 24/7 on-call rotation, 10% uplift in ARR. Includes 50k burst credits for spiky workloads.

Option B — Standard+ : 99.5% p99 latency target, 60-minute P1 response, business-hours on-call, no uplift (renewal pricing), 20k burst credits.

I recommend Option A only if you plan to expand peak queries 2x over the next 12 months — it keeps user-facing latency tight and reduces throttling risk. If you're mainly doing steady growth, Option B is conservative and keeps costs down.

Next steps: can you confirm which option you'd prefer by 2028-03-23? If you pick Option A, I'll route a short SLA addendum and a mutual action plan to procurement and legal for signature.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: SLA_Options_AX-8791.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@axiomhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@axiomhealth.com
Date: 2028-03-16T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Axiom Health — SLA & support upgrade options

Neha,

Thanks for the clear options. A couple of quick clarifications before we present to finance and security:
- For Option A, what is the crediting model if you miss the p99 SLO (monthly or quarterly)?
- Can you confirm whether the 15-minute P1 response includes an engineer on the phone or just acknowledgement / triage?
- We need the SOC 2 Type II attestation updated in the contract addendum — our security team flagged the current cert expires 2028-05-10.

I've attached our procurement header and PO terms (PO_Terms_AX.txt) to speed review.

If possible, can we get a mutual action plan and the proposed SLA addendum hooked into DocuSign so procurement can route internally?

Best,
Evan
Evan Liu
Head of Platform Ops, Axiom Health
ev an.liu@axiomhealth.com

Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-03-17T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Axiom Health — SLA & support upgrade options

Evan — appreciate the questions. Quick answers inline, then attached a mutual action plan and a draft SLA addendum.

- Crediting model: Financial credits are assessed monthly against missed SLOs; cumulative credits cap at 20% of monthly invoice. We can provide a quarterly rollup option if you'd prefer less noise (credits applied quarterly instead).
- P1 response: 15-minute acknowledgement + engineer on-call within 60 minutes for live troubleshooting. If you need immediate engineer phone involvement within 15 minutes, we can add a separate premium incident-handling add-on (rare).
- SOC 2: Our next audit window completes 2028-04-25; we will provide an updated SOC 2 attestation in the SLA addendum and commit to delivering before your renewal date.

Attached: Mutual_Action_Plan_AX-8791.docx (timeline and owners), SLA_Addendum_AX-8791.pdf (draft). I also created a DocuSign envelope template — I can send it as soon as you confirm Option A vs B and the final dollar figure.

Proposed timeline:
- 2028-03-23: Axiom confirms option
- 2028-03-27: Redwood finalizes addendum & DocuSign
- 2028-03-30: Procurement signature window

Let me know if you'd like a short call to walk legal/procurement through the credits language.

Thanks,
Neha

Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan_AX-8791.docx; SLA_Addendum_AX-8791.pdf
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-18T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: Axiom Health — SLA & support upgrade options

Team — forwarding the exchange with Axiom. They signaled interest in Option A (Premium SLO) but procurement needs clarity on credits and SOC 2 timing. Key points for approval:
- They're asking for p99 99.9% with 15-min P1 acknowledgement + 60-min on-call engineer; proposed pricing +10% ARR vs renewal.
- They're requesting the monthly crediting model with a 20% monthly cap.
- They would like 50k burst credits included.

Request: Can we grant a 20% one-time renewal discount (year 1) tied to a 12-month committed term if we include a 10% ARR uplift MSRP? This helps land the expansion while protecting unit economics. If finance/legal pushes back, I'd accept replacing the one-time discount with 10k additional burst credits.

Related: HubSpot deal AX-8791 shows expected close = 2028-03-30. Planning to send DocuSign if you both sign off.

—Neha

Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal: Axiom Health — SLA & support upgrade options

Neha,

I approve moving forward with Option A under the following conditions:
1) The 20% one-time renewal discount is authorization-limited to a maximum of two deals/month for our region — document in the renewal playbook.
2) Add a clause in the SLA addendum that allows us to convert the crediting cadence from monthly to quarterly with a minimum 30-day notice for the customer (reduces operational churn).
3) Finance needs a line item for burst credits separated from base ARR in the DocuSign so revenue recognition is clean.

If legal okays the SOC 2 delivery commitment by 2028-04-25, proceed. Otherwise grant the alternate concession of +10k burst credits instead of discount.

Ben Carter
